title: Harmonic sequence-length binner + kernel-aware microbatch shaping for pad reduction
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Reduce wasted padded tokens and improve GPU throughput by dynamically bucketing requests into harmonic sequence-length classes and shaping micro-batches according to kernel efficiency and prefill/decode scheduling. This ticket implements a kernel-aware harmonic binner + prefill-priority scheduler and couples it with light attention sparsity heuristics to reduce compute for long tails. Motivation: current static bucketing causes heavy pad inflation for conversational workloads with skewed seqlen distributions, especially on mixed short/prefill+decode traffic. We're targeting a >=30% reduction in padded token volume per request for typical customer workloads and measurable p99 latency regression <=5% under steady-state throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Production A/B shows >=30% reduction in padded tokens per request on sampled workloads (chat, search, summarization)
Tokens/sec per GPU improves by >=18% in end-to-end throughput tests with live trace replay
p99 latency at 95th percentile load does not regress by more than 5% versus baseline; no customer-visible errors introduced
Rollout plan validated with canary on dedicated pool and fallback to current bucketer on anomalies
implementation_notes: Design: 1) Introduce harmonic bucketing: compute harmonic bins (e.g., {8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256}) derived from empirical seqlen histogram and kernel sweet spots; map incoming requests to nearest harmonic bin but allow bin coalescing for sparsely populated ranges. 2) Kernel-aware scoring: each bin keeps kernel-affinity metadata (throughput/tokens-per-second per model variant) learned from microbenchmarks; pack microbatches respecting the fastest kernel for the dominant seqlen. 3) Prefill-priority scheduler: prefill requests (encoder-like long-context prefills) are prioritized into separate time-slices to avoid head-of-line padding for short decode requests; implement prefill tagging on RPC and a bounded prefill queue with backpressure hints. 4) Attention-sparsity heuristic: during prefill, enable block-sparse attention for layers above a threshold length when model supports it (quantized kernels only) to reduce matmul cost. 5) Metrics & safety: add pad_ratio, kernel_choice, prefill_wait_time, and per-bin p99 to the console dashboard and enable anomaly alerts. Implementation will touch request-router, microbatcher, kernel-selection logic, and runtime telemetry. Rollback: toggle via runtime feature-flag; can revert to legacy bucketer per pool. Note: avoid excessive fragmentation of bins — we cap at 8 active bins per worker to keep kernel cache hit rates high.
experimental_results: Local perf runs on trace replay (internal-chat-v2 sample): baseline padded_tokens_per_request=220, harmonic-binner padded_tokens_per_request=142 (35.5% reduction). Tokens/sec/GPU baseline=112k, experiment=136k (+21.4%). However observed a 7% increase in p99 latency in a synthetic mixed-load test due to prefill head-of-line under naive scheduling; mitigated by introducing prefill-priority time-slicing which reduced p99 regression to 3%. Kernel affinity logging showed that 72% of coalesced bins used the fwd-optimized FP16 kernel; remaining 28% used quantized int8 kernels with 1.8x lower throughput but lower memory pressure. Attention sparsity tests on GPT-like model reduced matmul FLOPs by ~12% for seqlen>512 but added ~3% end-to-end latency in short-tail requests when enabled globally; hence we gate sparsity to prefill-only for now.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive binning increases variance in latency and causes jitter. Mitigation: enforce max bin width and adaptive coalescing thresholds based on observed variance.
Risk: Kernel cache churn if bins change frequently. Mitigation: sticky bin assignments for a short TTL (e.g., 60s) and limit active bins per worker.
Risk: Prefill-priority may starve decodes at high prefill load. Mitigation: implement weighted time-slicing and backpressure signals to clients; canary rollout to validate policies.
Risk: Attention sparsity may cause quality regressions for some models. Mitigation: enable for model variants with validated quality tests and include eval harness checks before flag flip.
rollout_plan: 1) Lab validation with replay traces; 2) Canary on 5% of dedicated pools (non-production tenants) for 48h; 3) 10% traffic canary on low-risk customers with observability; 4) Gradual increase to 50% then 100% with monitoring gates; each step reversible via feature-flag. Add automated rollback if pad_ratio increases or p99 latency alarm fires above threshold.
